Signal: Tuesday's bank earnings (JPM $5.94, GS $12.44, C $2.41, WFC $1.85 consensus) and Wednesday's CPI - everything today is positioning for those. headlines.headline: Midday (noon ET): Dow +0.3 to +0.5%, S&P 500 roughly flat (~7,820.5, -0.04%, near record), Nasdaq -0.2 to -0.4% (QQQ -0.7%). Breadth is better than the index split: 9 of 11 S&P sectors up, ~330 stocks higher, energy leading (XLE +1.7%) and tech -1% the laggard. The chip skid is the day's real story - SOXX -2.5%, on track for a fifth straight down day; Deutsche Bank cut tech to neutral from overweight, arguing rotation has run too far even if Q3 earnings are strong.
headlines.why_it_matters: the index split masks healthy breadth ex-tech - this is a chip-led rotation, not a broad selloff; the Deutsche call gives the rotation a Wall Street stamp, so Tuesday's banks and Wednesday's CPI decide whether tech weakness is contained or spreads

headlines.headline: Oil bid firmed as Trump's Sunday 'energy ceasefire' unraveled: Brent +2%+ above $106 (two-week high), WTI +~2% to ~$93.60, after another tanker incident off Oman and with Moscow yet to confirm the deal (Zelensky says Russian strikes continued). XOM +~2% near its 176.41 buy point, CVX +1.5% in a buy zone, COP +~2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: the supply-risk premium is back in full - unconfirmed weekend diplomacy faded within hours, and energy is again the day's only clear momentum trade into Wednesday's CPI

headlines.headline: Microsoft recaptured a $4T market cap in early Monday trading (first time since Oct 29, 2025), within reach of its $4.029T all-time high; shares are up 50%+ from the June 2026 low, with D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria citing accelerating returns on AI spending. Carried: Barclays and Deutsche Bank both raised targets to $600 this morning (Phillip Securities downgraded to Neutral).
headlines.why_it_matters: a round-number milestone plus a bullish sell-side AI-spend-ROI narrative - positive sentiment flow on top of the $600 target raises; the session's clearest megacap counterpoint to the chip skid

headlines.headline: ICAP technical strategist Walter Zimmerman flags a 'big, bearish, rising wedge' on NVDA's 18-month weekly chart - waning upside momentum even as it made record highs; $210 daily to test the peak thesis, a monthly close below $204.84 as the first warning, below $185.94 'real problems'. Shares fell ~1% early, threatening a fourth straight down session.
headlines.why_it_matters: after a 26% six-month run, a named bearish technician gives profit-takers a narrative and price-anchors the downside - breaks of the stated levels become the near-term tape to watch into ASML/TSMC earnings

headlines.headline: Carried: Reflection AI tie-up structure taking shape (FT) - full acquisition, acqui-hire, or bigger investment; Nvidia already has ~$800M in; Reflection (ex-Google DeepMind founders) raised at ~$25B pre-money and launched the 501B-param open-weight Beam on Oct 5; the DOJ's reported Groq probe could favor an acqui-hire. Still FT-only reporting, unconfirmed by Nvidia.
headlines.why_it_matters: HN's 176-point thread reads it as 'commoditize your complement' - open models as hardware leverage over hyperscalers - but it's still one paper's story, single-source, unconfirmed by Nvidia - treat as fragile

headlines.headline: NHTSA disclosed a preliminary probe into robotaxis speeding in active school zones: a petitioner filed citing social-media videos; the Office of Defects Investigation will evaluate the claim covering ~1,000 Cybercab/Model Y 2026 vehicles, but has not yet ruled on whether to open a full investigation. TSLA fell 0.6% to ~$380, under its 200-day line. This is the second federal inquiry into the Cybercab since launch (the Sept self-certification probe sent the stock down 6% the next day). Carried: the company account confirmed 300+ Cybercabs in Austin (8x in 30 days) and named Dallas next; Cybercab at the Paris Motor Show Oct 12-18 (display only).
headlines.why_it_matters: a new safety headline can dent robotaxi-valuation momentum just as the fleet story got its first official scale number - but the probe is preliminary, not a full investigation, and EU approval (December homologation) plus the NHTSA Oct 30 sworn-certification deadline are the gating items

headlines.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald cut AMZN to $310 from $320 and Wells Fargo to $329 from $338 ahead of Q3 results (late Oct), both keeping Overweight - Wells expects Q3 ahead of consensus, AWS acceleration into Q4, and reiteration of the $220B 2026 capex guide, wanting detail on Amazon's consumer AI/agent strategy. Carried: WSJ's ~$7B Decart buyout talks - Decart valued ~$4B in May (PitchBook), Anthropic walked from a $6B deal after due diligence, Trainium 3 fit claimed - still single-source, neither company commented.
headlines.why_it_matters: targets trimmed but theses intact - more valuation haircut than thesis change, a mild sentiment drag on top of the single-source Decart overhang; the reaction will ride on whether Decart reads as smart verticalization or another multi-billion AI capex commitment

headlines.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald cut META to $840 from $860 (Overweight kept) - mild drag, thesis intact. Counterweight: Jim Cramer called META a 'monster long' on Menlo Ventures' Deedy Das Sensor Tower data - Muse Day-14 retention 22.5% vs ChatGPT's 26.8% ('almost as good as ChatGPT'), Day-7 above 30%, stronger Day-1 retention. Wrinkle: security researcher Patrick Wardle disclosed a macOS Muse zero-day (local apps grabbing auth tokens) - single-source, unconfirmed - possible sentiment offset. Carried: the retention bounce (+1.5%) vs HN's Oct 6 Muse security-dumpster-fire thread as the unpriced counterweight.
headlines.why_it_matters: the retention data is getting mainstream amplification (Cramer) which supports the bounce, but it's still one VC's post, single-source - treat the bounce size as fragile; the zero-day is a fresh single-source wrinkle, not confirmed

headlines.headline: Bleichmar Fonti & Auld announced via GlobeNewswire today a lead-plaintiff deadline of December 1, 2026 for the securities-fraud class action alleging Alphabet misrepresented Gemini 3.5 Pro development progress (the 4.4% drop on July 16, 2026) - the deadline date is new. Cantor reaffirmed Overweight, $420 PT today. Carried: TD Cowen's $485 target is the bull counterweight.
headlines.why_it_matters: formal deadline notices keep the lawsuit in the news cycle, pressuring sentiment - but this is routine plaintiff-firm marketing with no new facts alleged; the announcement is confirmed, the misconduct is alleged
